cases.name: Anthonya Lynnette "Thonya" Blevins
cases.about:
Anthony Lattimore, Blevins' brother, shared his grief and memories of his sister. "It's rough right now. It's going to be a process," Lattimore said. Lattimore described Blevins as his "twin," recalling her ability to calm him during tough times. "She was funny, man. She was funny. You know what I mean? She was never a negative person. It was always something positive about her," said Lattimore. He hopes people remember his sister for her positivity and love. "She was always smiling. She had the prettiest smile ever. And just remember the love that she used to share with everybody out here," Lattimore said.

Her obituary said, "Anthonya was a wonderful mother, daughter, sister, cousin, and friend. She was a beautiful spirit in every way. Her smile brightened every room she walked into, and her light was contagious. She was very family-oriented. Whether it was a holiday or just a family cookout, Anthonya was always orchestrating and bringing the family together. She was known for being a loving mother and the best cook-she prepared meals for all the family gatherings.
Anthonya was the most loving, giving, and caring person-she would give you her last without a second thought. If you asked her why, she would always say, "God provided for them through me, and He won't let me go without!"
She was happiest when she was with her family and listening to reggae music. She always saw the silver lining in every situation and had a Bible verse and a song for you to listen to, whether you asked for it or not. She would turn up the volume and say, "Listen to this!" while singing it to you. Anthonya uplifted and supported everyone around her, even while silently fighting her own battles."

cases.name: Alyssa Nicole "Ally" Hill
cases.about: She worked at Skyline Chili on Cincinnati, OH. Her Go Fund Me said: "Ally was a bright light in the world. Many knew her as a fierce, loving friend, a hardworking & devoted mom, and above all, someone who was kind to others and who loved everyone she knew unconditionally."
cases.narrative: He came in to the Chili's restaurant where she worked a little before noon as the restaurant was crowded for the lunch rush. According to prosecutors, Hill asked someone else to wait on him because she didn't want to have any contact with him. Prosecutors allege Wright ordered a glass of water and sat in booth for several minutes. "No conversation, no argument, there was nothing," prosecutors said in court. Prosecutors allege Wright then put on a "military style hat" and removed a large military knife from a sheath on his hip, pushed past several people and stabbed Ally in the chest and as she turned to flee, stabbed her again in the back.
